facts.t: One judgment ended the protection that let convicted MPs keep their seats
facts.d: Section 8(4) gave sitting legislators three months to appeal before disqualification bit. Lily Thomas (2013) struck it down — conviction now disqualifies immediately, appeal or no appeal.

facts.t: Courts cannot touch an election once it has begun
facts.d: N. P. Ponnuswami (1952) held that no court may interfere at any intermediate stage of the electoral process. The only route is an election petition after the result — which is why delays in deciding petitions matter so much.

facts.t: Kenya decides election petitions within six months, by constitutional command
facts.d: India has no equivalent deadline. Petitions here can outlast the term of the House they concern, rendering the remedy meaningless — the reason Election Tribunals keep being proposed.

bank.q: Lily Thomas (2013) struck down which provision?
bank.e: Section 8(4), which had allowed sitting legislators three months to appeal before disqualification took effect.

bank.q: With reference to disqualification under section 8, consider the following statements:
s: Conviction under specified laws disqualifies irrespective of the punishment imposed.
Under any other law, a minimum of two years' imprisonment is required.
The disqualification period is six years.
bank.e: All three are correct. Where only a fine is imposed the period runs from conviction; where imprisonment is imposed, from release.

bank.q: Match List I (section) with List II (ground of disqualification):
pairs: 1. Holding a commercial contract with the Union or State
2. Conviction for corrupt practices, decided by the President on ECI advice
bank.e: Section 8A for corrupt practices, 9 for dismissal, 9A for government contracts, and 10A for expense filings, which carries a three-year bar.

bank.q: Which one of the following distinguishes corrupt practices from electoral offences INCORRECTLY?
o: Corrupt practices are civil wrongs; electoral offences are criminal
Corrupt practices are tried by the High Court in an election petition
Corrupt practices are defined in section 123
bank.e: Electoral offences trigger disqualification only where specifically listed in section 8.

bank.rs: They can take years to decide, sometimes outlasting the term of the House concerned.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — hence the proposals for Election Tribunals and statutory deadlines on the Kenyan model.

bank.q: An election petition must be filed within:
bank.e: 45 days under section 81, before the High Court having jurisdiction under section 80A. The United Kingdom uses a stricter 21-day deadline.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about remedies:
s: A disqualification under section 8A carries no appeal but may be challenged by writ.
The Election Commission may remove or reduce a disqualification period under section 11.
A disqualified person is permanently barred from contesting again.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. There is no bar on re-election once the disqualification period ends.

bank.q: All of the following are global best practices cited EXCEPT:
o: The United Kingdom disqualifying those serving over one year in prison, without political discretion
Australia's automatic disqualification for offences carrying over a year's imprisonment
The Philippines giving its electoral body binding power to disqualify candidates
The United States requiring pre-clearance of all candidate nominations
bank.e: No such American practice is cited. The three models offered are Britain, Australia and the Philippines.

bank.q: Rajbala v. State of Haryana (2015) held that the right to contest elections is:
o: A natural right subject to reasonable restriction
bank.e: Not a fundamental right — a statutory right conferred and limited by the Representation of the People Act.

bank.q: With reference to case law on corrupt practices, consider the following:
s: An appeal to vote on the basis of the candidate's language is a corrupt practice.
Promoting hatred against the government is a corrupt practice.
There must be a nexus between gifts and inducement to vote.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Pritpal Singh held that hatred against the government is not a corrupt practice — only hatred against classes of citizens is.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
bank.e: N. P. Ponnuswami (1952) → Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975) → Lily Thomas (2013) → Lok Prahari (2018).

bank.q: An appeal from a High Court decision on an election petition lies to the Supreme Court under:
bank.e: Section 116A provides a statutory appeal, distinct from the discretionary special leave jurisdiction.
